outcomes.description: The book is moved behind the flower.
outcomes.target: The book is visibly positioned behind the flower, with the flower in front of it.

nodes.question: Is the source book—the blue-covered book with a tan page block—visibly positioned behind any flower in the edited image?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the object identifiable as the source book is visibly behind a flower, with the flower in front of and occluding it. Fail if the source book is identifiable and the image clearly shows it is not behind any flower. Unknown if the source book's identity or the relative depth/occlusion cannot be determined. Do not identify a separate pale object as the book without visual evidence that it is the source book.
nodes.binding: Compare the source book's distinctive blue cover and tan page block with objects in the edited image, then assess only its depth relation to the flower(s). Require foreground/occlusion evidence; proximity or left/right placement alone does not establish that the book is behind a flower.

nodes.question: Does the edited image show clear progress toward placing the source book behind a flower, even if the placement is incomplete?
nodes.criteria: Pass only if the source book is identifiable and visible evidence shows movement toward the requested depth relation, such as partial overlap with a flower visibly in front of the book, without establishing complete fulfillment. Fail if the source book is identifiable and clearly remains separate from the flowers with no evidence of progress toward that relation. Unknown if identity, depth, or progress cannot be determined. Mere proximity, lateral repositioning, or unrelated changes to the book or flowers are not progress.
nodes.binding: Use the source book's blue cover and tan page block to distinguish it from other objects. Compare its relation to all visible flowers; require evidence consistent with the book moving behind a flower, not mere closeness or left/right placement. Preserve unknown for genuinely indeterminate visual evidence.

nodes.question: Is the book visibly positioned behind the flower?
nodes.criteria: Apply the original rubric to R1 using s1 and s2. Complete (yes) if s1 passes. Partial if s1 does not pass and s2 passes. Absent (no) if both checks fail. Unknown if neither check passes and at least one is unknown; unresolved evidence must remain unknown. Do not count unrelated edits as progress.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

response.content: {"accepted":false,"reason":"The fulfillment rule can misclassify unresolved evidence as absent: it says “Absent (no) if both checks fail” without requiring that the checks establish no requested progress across the relevant evidence. In particular, s1 can fail because the book is not fully behind a flower while s2 fails because progress is not established; those failures do not necessarily prove no progress. The rubric requires insufficient evidence to remain unresolved, so the readout must not treat these failures as sufficient evidence for no."}

parsed.reason: The fulfillment rule can misclassify unresolved evidence as absent: it says “Absent (no) if both checks fail” without requiring that the checks establish no requested progress across the relevant evidence. In particular, s1 can fail because the book is not fully behind a flower while s2 fails because progress is not established; those failures do not necessarily prove no progress. The rubric requires insufficient evidence to remain unresolved, so the readout must not treat these failures as sufficient evidence for no.
